AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring certain financially

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1948

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring certain finan-
cially assisted development projects in a city with a population of one
million or more to be subject to certain prevailing wage requirements

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to ensure that financially assisted develop-
ment projects in New York City are subject to Section 220 of the Labor
Law, including requirements for prevailing wage.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill would amend section 220 of the New York State
Labor Law to define covered projects in New York City and ensure that
such projects are subject to requirements for the payment of prevailing
wage.

Section 2 would establish the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would require certain public benefit corporations, local
development corporations and other economic development entities that
provide or administer public financial assistance to be covered by
prevailing wage requirements under the New York State Labor Law. This
would include third parties acting on behalf of these economic develop-
ment entities. The New York State Constitution requires that prevailing
wage be paid to workers on public work projects, so as not to undermine
the cost of local labor. Unfortunately, too many employers avoid paying
their workers prevailing wage because the financing on these projects
comes in many different forms and through a myriad of quasi-public enti-
ties. This bill would ensure that, in such cases, such entities that
seek to secure public financing and achieve operational flexibility are
not able to circumvent the constitutional requirement of prevailing
wages.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
